fetch.step: harness `corpus fetch`, networked, separate from every run (AQP6:213; HD:1117-1135)
fetch.source: url at commit: a shallow single-commit fetch by SHA, no checkout, no hooks, no filters, LFS smudge off, submodules not materialized
verify: the fetched commit equals commit, and its git tree SHA-1 equals gitTree

fetch.onMismatch: refuse; the entry is not admitted to the store

treeDigestAlgorithm.definition: QD-22 (HD:1126). Let A be the array, over every entry of `git ls-tree -r --full-tree <commit>` whose type is blob (modes 100644, 100755 and 120000), of [path, mode, h]: path is the full path as a UTF-8 string; mode is the six-digit octal string git prints; h is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the raw blob bytes (a symlink's bytes are its target text, an LFS pointer's are the pointer text). A is sorted by path bytes. treeDigest is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of A under CAN:67-74 (json.dumps with ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators (',', ':')).
treeDigestAlgorithm.gitlinks: Gitlinks (mode 160000) have no content and are not in A. Each is listed in submodulePolicy.gitlinks with its pinned commit, and gitTree binds it.
treeDigestAlgorithm.byteLimit: Lead reading: CAN's 4 MiB admission limit applies to admitted records, not to this digest preimage, which is streamed. Two preimages exceed it: aws-cdk (5,942,722 bytes; canonical() refuses it with BYTE_LIMIT) and aws-sdk-rust (35,318,302 bytes over 245,250 blobs).
treeDigestAlgorithm.crossCheck: Every value comes from a streaming implementation. A second implementation (a fresh fetch, per-blob `git cat-file blob`, and the foundation canonical(), or for aws-cdk the same serializer without the byte limit) gave identical values for anyhow, hyper, deno, webpack, zustand and aws-cdk, which cover symlinks, gitlinks, LFS pointers and an over-limit preimage.

contentDigestAlgorithm.definition: SHA-256 over the concatenation, in ascending byte order of path, of: '<mode> <type> <h> ' + path + NUL, for every entry of `git ls-tree -r --full-tree <commit>`. For a blob, h is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the raw blob bytes (symlink blobs hash their target text; LFS pointers hash the pointer bytes). For a gitlink (type commit), h is the recorded commit SHA-1.
contentDigestAlgorithm.why: The git tree SHA-1 pins the commit's tree, and this SHA-256 adds a collision-resistant check over the same bytes.

sizeMethod.classBoundaries: Integer intervals read from AQP6:224 ('small (< 20k lines), medium (20k-200k), large (200k-1M) and very large (> 1M)'): the strict bounds '< 20k' and '> 1M' are kept literally, so 20,000 is medium and 1,000,000 is large; the shared endpoint 200,000 goes to large, the same lower-inclusive reading as 20,000. T2a's table had very-large '>= 1,000,000' (GROK2 NBO-1). No entry lies on a boundary.
sizeMethod.unit: physical lines (newline count, plus one for a final unterminated line) of git blobs at the pinned commit; symlink blobs are not source files and are not counted (T2a counted each as one line)
sizeMethod.basis: hand-written lines of the entry's languageGroup: rust=.rs; tsjs=.ts .tsx .mts .cts .js .jsx .mjs .cjs (incl. .d.ts); python=.py .pyi; polyglot=rust+tsjs. sizeClass is the class of that basis.
sizeMethod.perLanguageClass: languageClasses gives each language group's own hand-written lines and class. The per-language counts (counts) use it, so a polyglot entry counts toward Rust at the class of its Rust lines and toward TS/JS at the class of its TS/JS lines (T2a counted it at the combined class).
sizeMethod.vendored: a path segment in {vendor, vendored, _vendor, third_party, third-party, node_modules, bower_components}, or root .gitattributes linguist-vendored
sizeMethod.generated: not vendored, and either a path rule (a path segment in {generated, __generated__, gen, codegen-out}, a .generated./.gen. name, *.min.js, or root .gitattributes linguist-generated) or generatedMarkerRule

generatedMarkerRule.scope: the first 1,024 bytes of the blob, matched case-insensitively
markers: M3-M6 only at the start of a comment line: optional blanks, one comment leader (// /// //! /* /** * # <!-- -- """ '''), optional blanks, then
M3: [this file|code|module|class is|was|has been] + auto-generated | autogenerated | auto generated | automatically generated | machine-generated
M4: [this file|code|module|class is|was|has been | code] + generated by|from|with|using|via
M5: this file|code|module|class is|was|has been generated

M6: <one token of [A-Za-z0-9_@./-]> generated code, where the token is not a common English word (the, this, that, these, a, an, all, any, some, our, its, their, such, no, of, for, in, on, from, and, or, by, to, with, is, are)
generatedMarkerRule.replaces: T2a's rule (rule 1), which matched '@generated|generated code|Code generated .* DO NOT EDIT|DO NOT EDIT|auto-generated|autogenerated|This file was automatically generated|Generated by' case-insensitively anywhere in the first KiB, so prose such as 'a signal generated by CTRL+C' counted (GROK2 NBO-2).

sizeMethod.testOrExample: reported, not excluded: a path segment in {tests, test, __tests__, testing, fixtures, __fixtures__, examples, example, benches, bench, docs_src, e2e, playground, spec, __snapshots__, testdata} or a test_/.test./.spec./_test name
sizeMethod.limitations: Heuristic classifier. Per-entry overrides are recorded in sizeBasis.classOverride and notes. Known residue: generated files without a header marker count as hand-written (aws-sdk-rust, aws-sdk-js-v3 clients/), and .yarn/releases bundles count as hand-written JS.

tagMethod: shapeTags are computed from the tree (see shapeEvidence): rs-cfg-feature-heavy = at least 15 #[cfg(/#[cfg_attr(/cfg!( sites per 1,000 hand-written Rust lines, or at least 75 [features] entries across Cargo manifests; js-mixed-cjs-esm = non-test hand-written .js/.cjs/.mjs files include both CommonJS (require(, module.exports, exports.x) and ESM (import/export statements); TS/JS tags apply only to tsjs and polyglot entries. shapeTagsJudged are lead judgements for review. T2b: cfg sites and JS module styles are counted over files that are hand-written under generatedMarkerRule 2. polyglot-rust-tsjs is measured on any entry with more than 1,000 hand-written Rust lines and more than 10,000 hand-written TS/JS lines (sui and vscode carry it); languageGroup, not the tag, decides what is counted.

familyRules.source: HD §5.3 (DESIGN-r13:511-523), QD-12: repositories share an independence family when one is a fork, mirror, vendored copy or split of another; they share generated code from the same generator; they are parts of one multi-checkout workspace; or they share an upstream project. Sharing an organization alone does not merge.
readings: Shared generator merges when the generator's output is a material part of one repository (aws-sdk-rust, aws-sdk-js-v3, node-rs); generated glue under 1% of a repository's analyzed lines is recorded in notMerged, not merged.
Families are the transitive closure of the grounds below (union-find).
A family is wholly held-out or wholly dev; the builder refuses a mixed family.
familyRules.sharedBlobCheck: Every pair of the 49 corpus repositories was compared for byte-identical blobs (same git blob SHA) among Rust, TS/JS and Python files of 3 or more lines, in any path and class. sharedBlobPairs lists every pair that shares any. Overlap is material, and a vendored-copy ground, when it reaches 1,000 lines or 1% (10,000 ppm) of the smaller repository's analyzed lines. Below that it is boilerplate or a copied fixture, and it is recorded in notMerged. Held-out repositories share at most 16 lines with any other repository (vitest/vite).
